findings.reason: the wrong locus sends §8's node at a fallback constructor while the CLI's own construction and the per-batch pass-through, which is what overspent USD 6.26 against a USD 5.00 cap, is untouched; the section's stubbed done-when passes either way, so only the locus sentence governs where the node works.
findings.text: §8 states "The repair belongs where the drain's `CampaignBudget` is built for an apply (`harmonize.py` ~1099)", but that line is the `CampaignBudget` import and `harmonize.py:1106` (`budget = budget or CampaignBudget()`) is only the fallback used when no budget is passed; the live apply builds it at `imas_codex/cli/sn.py:6164` (`CampaignBudget(per_batch_cost_cap=cost_limit, campaign_cost_ceiling=cost_limit)`) and the defect — each batch receiving the whole cap — is at `imas_codex/standard_names/campaign.py:1016` (`drain_fn(run_id, self.budget.per_batch_cost_cap)`), so a node repairing at ~1099 changes a default the production path never reaches and the per-batch split stays intact

findings.reason: the recorded costs already exist as `LLMCost` rows (`budget.py` phase `generate|regen|review_docs`), so the node can locate both the constant and a graph reader from the done-when alone; pinning the reader would tidy the section without changing what it builds.
findings.text: §12 asks the estimator to read "the recorded per-call spend of recent documentation regenerations and of the reviews that follow them" but names no reader for those records (the constant it replaces is `ESTIMATED_DOC_CALL_COST_USD`, `harmonize.py:758`, consumed in the dry-run branch at `imas_codex/cli/sn.py:6146`), unlike §8, §10 and §11 which each name a callable or a file
